_about: UK AND US ETHNICITY DO NOT SHARE A CANONICAL, for the same reason income does
not: they are different social classifications, not coarse and fine versions of
one. 'Hispanic' is a separate axis from race in the US and is not a UK category
at all; 'White British' versus 'Any other White background' is central in the UK
and absent from the US schemes.
This was tried the other way first, on 5 Oct 2026, by running
scripts/persona_harmonise.py over every scheme at once. It produced a canonical
of four values including 'Other or Asian or Hispanic' — merging three distinct
groups because one scheme's residual swallowed them — and in doing so DEGRADED
the US layer, which until then had Hispanic as a category of its own. That is
the union rule working correctly on the wrong question. Reverted.
The UK side uses the ONS five-group classification, which is the official UK
standard and is what the detailed schemes roll up into by construction. Two
studies ship the five groups directly; two ship the 18/19-category detail, whose
categories are strict subsets of the five. Nothing is lost that was collected.
'White' is the one label both layers map to. The concepts genuinely match there
and splitting it would assert a difference that does not exist.
Chinese sits under Asian, per the 2011 ONS classification onwards (it was Other
before 2011); both detailed schemes here are 2011-or-later. Arab sits under
Other, per ONS.
uk_k7tw5_osf (26 Oct 2026, IMG02): ONS-2011-style detailed labels from the k7tw5 snack warning-label study.
Eleven labels were already mapped by other schemes and keep that mapping; the seven new ones were classified by Jev
(category_concept, confidence 0.78-1.0) and reviewed. Jev flagged "Any other mixed/multiple ethnic group background" as
the residual; overruled, the residual is "Any other ethnic group". No canonical value added; no other scheme changed.
uk_pr8zu_osf (28 Oct 2026, IMG01): the k7tw5 lab's alcohol sibling. Its 18 labels are the same strings as uk_k7tw5_osf's
(checked by set equality in code), so the mapping is copied and no new judgement was needed. No canonical value added.
uk_3krjz_osf (29 Oct 2026, IMG48): ONS-2011-style 16-category labels from the Winton Centre flood risk-matrix survey, its
own spelling ("Carribean") kept. Jev (category_concept) put every label in its ONS group (white, mixed, asian, black at
0.72-1.0); the within-group catch-alls "Other White" / "Other Mixed" / "Other Asian" / "Other Black" scored residual
0.43-0.58 and go to their own group, as uk_ons_detailed_2011's "Any other ... background" labels do; "Any other ethnic
group" (residual 0.92) is Other ethnic group. No canonical value added; no other scheme changed.
uk_wsqyn_osf (29 Oct 2026, IMG34): the 18 ONS-2021-style options of the Restrain Food Database validation study (Cardiff),
word-for-word from its .qsf. Jev (category_concept) put every label in its ONS group (white 0.76-0.98, mixed 0.94-1.0, asian
0.85-1.0, black 0.66-0.99; Arab middle_eastern 0.99, which UK schemes file under Other ethnic group per ONS). The within-group
catch-alls scored residual 0.41-0.62 and go to their own group, as uk_ons_detailed_2021's do; 'Any other ethnic group'
(residual 0.93) is Other ethnic group. Labels shared with other schemes keep their mapping. No canonical value added.
